```{r setup_load}
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(viridis)
library(here)

# --- CONFIGURATION ---
SITES <- c("DE-HoH", "CA-Man", "AU-Sam", "KR-CRK", "US-ICh")
KEEP_VARS <- c("TIMESTAMP_START", "TA_F", "SW_IN_F", "VPD_F", "P_F", 
               "NETRAD", "G_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS", "H_F_MDS_QC", 
               "LE_F_MDS", "LE_F_MDS_QC", "NEE_VUT_REF", "NEE_VUT_REF_QC", 
               "GPP_NT_VUT_REF", "RECO_NT_VUT_REF")

# Function to load and clean data from ZIPs
load_flux_data <- function(site_id) {
  zip_path <- list.files(here::here("data", "raw"), 
                         pattern = paste0("_", site_id, "_FLUXNET_.*\\.zip$"), 
                         full.names = TRUE)
  if(length(zip_path) == 0) return(NULL)
  
  zz <- unzip(zip_path[1], list = TRUE)
  hh_file <- zz$Name[grep("FLUXMET_HH", zz$Name)]
  
  df <- read.csv(unzip(zip_path[1], files = hh_file), 
                 na.strings = "-9999", 
                 colClasses = c(TIMESTAMP_START = "character"))
  
  available_vars <- intersect(colnames(df), KEEP_VARS)
  df <- df[, available_vars]
  
  df <- df %>% 
    mutate(time = as.POSIXct(TIMESTAMP_START, format = "%Y%m%d%H%M", tz = "UTC"), 
           site = site_id) %>% 
    select(-TIMESTAMP_START)
  return(df)
}

# Load all site data into one dataframe
all_data <- map_df(SITES, load_flux_data)

# Load snapshot for metadata
snapshot_file <- list.files(here::here("data", "snapshots"), 
                            pattern = "snapshot.*\\.csv", 
                            full.names = TRUE)[1]
snapshot <- read.csv(snapshot_file, colClasses = "character")

tower_info <- snapshot %>% 
  filter(site_id %in% SITES) %>% 
  select(site_id, site_name, igbp, location_lat, location_long, first_year, last_year, data_hub, product_citation) %>% 
  rename(ID = site_id, Name = site_name, IGBP = igbp, 
         Lat = location_lat, Lon = location_long, 
         Start = first_year, End = last_year, Hub = data_hub, Citation = product_citation)
```

## **C1. SITE OVERVIEW**

The five towers were downloaded using the FLUXNET Shuttle. The snapshot file snapshot.csv records the downloaded metadata. The analysis is based on the corresponding ZIP archives (e.g., _DE-HoH_FLUXNET...zip), containing the half-hourly FLUXMET_HH data. The processing includes quality control and the selection of specific variables for flux analysis.

```{r setup_overview}
#| echo: true
kable(tower_info, caption = "Overview of analyzed FLUXNET sites") %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))
```

```{r setup_worldmap}
#| echo: true
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
tower_coords <- tower_info %>% 
  mutate(Lat = as.numeric(Lat), Lon = as.numeric(Lon))

ggplot(data = world) + 
  geom_sf(fill = "antiquewhite") + 
  geom_point(data = tower_coords, aes(x = Lon, y = Lat, color = IGBP), size = 4) + 
  geom_text(data = tower_coords, aes(x = Lon, y = Lat, label = ID), vjust = -1, size = 3) + 
  labs(title = "Geographical Distribution of Selected Flux Towers", color = "IGBP Class") + 
  theme_minimal()
```

## **C2. DATA COVERAGE**

Share of half hours per site and year in which NEE was measured (NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0) and not gap-filled.

```{r setup_coverage}
#| echo: true
coverage <- all_data %>% 
  mutate(year = year(time)) %>% 
  group_by(site, year) %>% 
  summarise(measured_share = mean(NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

ggplot(coverage, aes(x = year, y = site, fill = measured_share)) + 
  geom_tile(colour = "white") + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) + 
  labs(title = "Share of Measured NEE (QC=0) per Site and Year", 
       x = "Year", y = "Site ID", fill = "Measured Share") + 
  theme_minimal()
```

## **C3. SUMMARY STATISTICS**

Mean, minimum, maximum and share of missing half hours for each site. For precipitation (P_F), the Mean row gives the mean annual sum (mm per year).


```{r setup_summary_stats}
#| echo: true
#| results: "asis"
vars_labels <- c(TA_F = "TA_F (°C)", SW_IN_F = "SW_IN_F (W m⁻²)", VPD_F = "VPD_F (hPa)", 
                 P_F = "P_F (mm)", NEE_VUT_REF = "NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)", 
                 GPP_NT_VUT_REF = "GPP (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)", 
                 RECO_NT_VUT_REF = "RECO (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)", 
                 H_F_MDS = "H (W m⁻²)", LE_F_MDS = "LE (W m⁻²)")

# General statistics – ensure sentinel "-9999" is treated as missing
stats_long <- all_data %>%
  select(site, all_of(names(vars_labels))) %>%
  # Coerce to numeric (in case columns were read as character) and replace -9999 with NA
  mutate(across(all_of(names(vars_labels)), ~as.numeric(.x))) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(names(vars_labels)), ~na_if(.x, -9999))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-site, names_to = "var") %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    `% missing` = 100 * mean(is.na(value)),
    .by = c(site, var)
  )

# Annual precipitation mean sum
p_annual <- all_data %>%
  mutate(year = year(time)) %>%
  summarise(p_sum = sum(P_F, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(site, year)) %>%
  summarise(p_annual = mean(p_sum), .by = site)

stats_final <- stats_long %>%
  left_join(p_annual, by = "site") %>%
  mutate(Mean = if_else(var == "P_F", p_annual, Mean)) %>%
  select(-p_annual)

# Tables per site – render as HTML tables with styling
for (s in SITES) {
  # Use a level‑2 markdown heading for the site name (no extra spaces or asterisks)
  cat("\n\n## ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  tab <- stats_final %>%
    filter(site == s) %>%
    select(-site) %>%
    mutate(var = vars_labels[var]) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(Mean, Min, Max, `% missing`), names_to = "Statistic") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = value)
  # Output the HTML table as raw markup (results: "asis")
  cat(
    knitr::kable(tab, digits = 1, format = "html") %>%
      kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
  )
}
```


## **C4. TIME SERIES**

Comparison of daily Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE), Gross Primary Production (GPP), and Ecosystem Respiration (RECO). Values are converted to g C m⁻² d⁻¹.


```{r setup_time_series}
#| echo: true
#| fig.height: 9   # taller plot for clearer vertical spacing
    # Prepare daily fluxes, convert units and clean unrealistic RECO values for DE‑HoH
    daily_flux <- all_data %>%
      # Convert sentinel -9999 to NA for the three flux columns before any averaging
      mutate(across(c(NEE_VUT_REF, GPP_NT_VUT_REF, RECO_NT_VUT_REF), ~na_if(.x, -9999))) %>%
      mutate(date = as.Date(time)) %>%
      group_by(site, date) %>%
      summarise(
        across(c(NEE_VUT_REF, GPP_NT_VUT_REF, RECO_NT_VUT_REF),
                ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.0378),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(NEE_VUT_REF, GPP_NT_VUT_REF, RECO_NT_VUT_REF),
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(variable = recode(variable,
                            NEE_VUT_REF = "NEE",
                            GPP_NT_VUT_REF = "GPP",
                            RECO_NT_VUT_REF = "RECO")) %>%
  # Remove extreme RECO outliers for DE‑HoH (abs > 5000)
  mutate(value = ifelse(site == "DE-HoH" & variable == "RECO" & abs(value) > 5000,
                       NA_real_, value))

# Determine global y‑axis limits from the daily data (after outlier removal)
y_min <- floor(min(daily_flux$value, na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10
y_max <- ceiling(max(daily_flux$value, na.rm = TRUE) / 10) * 10

ggplot(daily_flux, aes(x = date, y = value, colour = variable)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  # Stack the five site plots vertically
  facet_wrap(~site, ncol = 1, scales = "fixed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(GPP = "darkgreen", RECO = "darkorange", NEE = "black")) +
  # Use a modest number of tick marks (pretty breaks) for a cleaner axis
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min, y_max),
                     breaks = pretty(daily_flux$value, n = 5),
                     labels = function(x) sprintf("%d", x)) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = expression(g~C~m^{-2}~d^{-1}), colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```


## **C5. DIURNAL CYCLES**

Seasons were defined based on month and latitude. For the Northern Hemisphere, spring is March-May, summer June-August, autumn September-November, and winter December-February. Sites in the Southern Hemisphere (if any) have their months shifted by six.

```{r setup_diurnal}
#| echo: true
season_nh <- c("Winter", "Winter", "Spring", "Spring", "Spring", "Summer", 
               "Summer", "Summer", "Autumn", "Autumn", "Autumn", "Winter")

variable_labels <- c(
  "NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)" = "NEE~(mu*mol~CO[2]~m^{-2}~s^{-1})",
  "LE (W m⁻²)" = "LE~(W~m^{-2})"
)

  # Prepare diurnal averages for each variable
  diurnal <- all_data %>%
    # Convert sentinel -9999 to NA for all relevant columns before averaging
    mutate(across(c(NEE_VUT_REF, GPP_NT_VUT_REF, RECO_NT_VUT_REF, LE_F_MDS), ~na_if(.x, -9999))) %>%
    left_join(tower_info %>% select(site = ID, lat = Lat), by = "site") %>%
    mutate(month = as.integer(format(time, "%m")),
           month_adj = if_else(lat < 0, (month + 5) %% 12 + 1, month),
           season = factor(season_nh[month_adj],
                           levels = c("Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", "Winter")),
           hour = as.numeric(format(time, "%H")) + as.numeric(format(time, "%M")) / 60) %>%
    summarise(`NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)` = mean(NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE),
              `LE (W m⁻²)` = mean(LE_F_MDS, na.rm = TRUE),
              .by = c(site, season, hour))

  diurnal %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(site, season, hour), names_to = "variable") %>%
  ggplot(aes(hour, value, colour = site)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  # Use custom labeller to give each facet its own y‑axis label
  facet_grid(
  variable ~ season,
  scales = "free_y",
  switch = "y",
  labeller = labeller(
    variable = as_labeller(variable_labels, default = label_parsed)
  )
) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Hour of day (local standard time)",
       y = NULL,
       colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", legend.position = "top")
```


## **C6. MY READING**
### **Energy balance (DE‑HoH)**

Analysis of the energy balance closure at the DE-HoH site. Only half-hours where both H and LE were measured (_QC == 0) are used.


```{r setup_energy_balance}
#| echo: true
# Convert sentinel -9999 to NA for the variables used in the energy‑balance plot
eb <- all_data %>%
  # ensure missing flags are true NA
  mutate(across(c(NETRAD, G_F_MDS, H_F_MDS, LE_F_MDS), ~na_if(.x, -9999))) %>%
  filter(site == "DE-HoH", H_F_MDS_QC == 0, LE_F_MDS_QC == 0) %>%
  mutate(available = NETRAD - G_F_MDS,
         turbulent = H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS) %>%
  filter(!is.na(available), !is.na(turbulent))

fit <- lm(turbulent ~ available, data = eb)
slope <- coef(fit)[["available"]]

ggplot(eb, aes(available, turbulent)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "blue", se = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5,
           label = paste0("slope = ", round(slope, 2), " (n = ", nrow(eb), ")")) +
  labs(x = expression(NETRAD - G~(W~m^{-2})),
       y = expression(H + LE~(W~m^{-2}))) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```



### **Comparison between towers**

```{r setup_comparison}
#| echo: true
# Convert sentinel -9999 to NA for all variables used in the summary tables
clean_all <- all_data %>%
  mutate(across(c(NEE_VUT_REF, GPP_NT_VUT_REF, RECO_NT_VUT_REF,
                  NETRAD, G_F_MDS, H_F_MDS, LE_F_MDS,
                  NEE_VUT_REF_QC), ~na_if(.x, -9999)))

annual_nee <- clean_all %>%
  mutate(year = year(time)) %>%
  summarise(nee_sum = sum(NEE_VUT_REF * 1800 * 12.011e-6, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(site, year)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(nee_sum)) %>%
  summarise(`Mean annual NEE (g C m⁻² yr⁻¹)` = mean(nee_sum),
            `Complete years` = n(), .by = site)

seasonal_gpp <- clean_all %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(time), month = month(date)) %>%
  group_by(site, month) %>%
  summarise(gpp = mean(GPP_NT_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  summarise(`GPP seasonal amplitude (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)` = max(gpp) - min(gpp), .by = site)

gap_filled <- clean_all %>%
  summarise(`Gap-filled NEE (%)` = 100 * mean(!(NEE_VUT_REF_QC %in% 0)), .by = site)

comparison <- annual_nee %>%
  left_join(seasonal_gpp, by = "site") %>%
  left_join(gap_filled, by = "site") %>%
  rename(Site = site)

kable(comparison, digits = 1) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```


> The strongest carbon uptake (most negative mean annual NEE) is observed at the **DE‑HoH** tower (‑254 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹). This tower also has the longest record (12 complete years) and a relatively high share of gap‑filled NEE values (≈ 69 %). The high uptake is likely driven by the temperate forest ecosystem, which efficiently absorbs CO₂ during the growing season.
>
> The **AU‑Sam** site shows a substantial uptake (‑128 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) despite a shorter record (8 years) and a similar gap‑filled proportion (≈ 68 %). Its moderate GPP seasonal amplitude (≈ 5 g C m⁻² d⁻¹) suggests a relatively stable photosynthetic period.
>
> **CA‑Man** exhibits the weakest uptake among the negative sites (‑22 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) with 15 complete years and a comparable gap‑filled share (≈ 69 %). The low GPP amplitude (≈ 4.8 g C m⁻² d⁻¹) indicates limited seasonal variation, which may reflect the Mediterranean climate of the site.
>
> The **KR‑CRK** tower is close to carbon neutral (≈ +1 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) and shows the largest GPP seasonal amplitude (≈ 10.8 g C m⁻² d⁻¹), implying strong seasonal productivity swings typical for a temperate monsoon region.
>
> Finally, **US‑ICh** is a net carbon source (+23 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹) even though it has the longest record (19 years). Its high gap‑filled NEE share (≈ 78 %) and the lowest GPP amplitude (≈ 3 g C m⁻² d⁻¹) suggest that measurement gaps and a relatively flat productivity curve limit carbon uptake.
>
> Across all sites, the share of gap‑filled NEE values ranges from ~ 64 % (KR‑CRK) to ~ 78 % (US‑ICh), highlighting the importance of data completeness when interpreting the carbon balance.
